items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] So, today I know that there is a group, the Hoofers, that you are the senior member of. Sandman Sims, Raymond Kailen, Jimmy Sly, Harold Kromer, Bernard Manners, the youngest member of the group.

ctx.x: Well, the one thing I noticed though is that tap dancing isn't really being passed on like it used to be in the old days. Some of the old masters used to have protégés, and the dancers of today don't have proteges like they used to. How do you account for that?

Well, that's because they don't buddy-buddy. They don't fraternize enough with -- well, there's one that does it. I think he's -- what did -- George Nuremberg, that's Nipsy Russell's protégé. Sandman. I think he has done this, Sandman Sims, see. Because -- do you understand? He is a Hooper, you know. You see, they're on-the-town dancer, you see. He has an idol also.
Well, maybe it's just that a tap -- tap dancing today for the young people doesn't have relevance like it did in the older days.
